disposition_reason: Reports cadmium, chromium, copper, lead and zinc by flame AAS in ajwain, black cumin, coriander and fenugreek from local markets in three Central Gondar districts; cadmium and lead were not detected.

study.design: market survey of locally grown spices
study.origin: grown in East Dembia, West Dembia and Takusa districts, Central Gondar Zone, Ethiopia
study.market: three local markets per district (nine markets)
study.method: washed, oven-dried 60 C, HNO3/HClO4 digestion at 240 C, flame AAS
lod: method LOD Cd 0.036, Cr 0.12, Cu 0.064, Pb 0.22, Zn 0.26 mg/L (text); instrument detection limits Cd 0.01, Cr 0.05, Cu 0.005, Pb 0.04, Zn 0.005 mg/L (Table 2)
study.qa: no CRM; spike recoveries Cr 92.08-107.13%, Cu 94.97-98.0%, Zn 92.6-96.6%; Cd and Pb recoveries printed ND; reagent blanks; RSD < 10%

unresolved: Two fenugreek copper cells repeat the adjacent coriander zinc cells (West Dembia 14.24 ± 3.497; Takusa 11.08/11.083 ± 1.918), suggesting a transcription error; recorded as printed with notes.
Text says the highest copper was in coriander at Takusa (30.30), but Table 4 places 30.30 under West Dembia coriander.
Cd and Pb spike recoveries are printed as ND, so recovery for the two metals of main interest is unverified.
Sampling dates not reported; per-site n is 12 purchased samples composited per market, analyzed in triplicate.
